note: Replace each `url` below with a Stripe Payment Link from the parish Stripe dashboard, then set `configured` to true. Payment Links are public URLs — never place a Stripe secret key (sk_live_… / sk_test_…) in this repository.

demo.note: Renders an interactive mock of the checkout so the parish can review the donor experience and compare providers before committing. No card is ever charged and no payment API is called. `publishableKey` is Stripe's own sample TEST key from their public documentation; publishable keys are designed to be readable by anyone and cannot move money. Set `enabled` to false to hide the mock.

zelle.note: Zelle has no payment links, so nothing here can be a clickable button. Three things can be published, all optional. `tag` is a Zelle tag (a business handle like StElizabethOrthodox), which is the friendliest option and is set up in the parish bank app; it is preferred over `handle` when both are present. `handle` is the email address or U.S. mobile number enrolled with the parish bank account. `qr` is a site-relative path to the QR code image exported from the parish bank app, e.g. /assets/img/zelle-qr.png — it MUST be the bank-issued code, because the QR encodes a Zelle directory token that cannot be generated from an email address. Leave a value empty and its row is hidden rather than invented.

providersNote: Comparison data for the provider selector on the Giving page. Cursory analysis, September 2026, verified against vendor documentation rather than live accounts — see docs/giving-setup.md. `status` drives the colour: yes / no / partial / info. `capabilities.recurring` drives the form itself: "yes" offers a monthly option, "no" removes it, and "donor-scheduled" offers it but explains that the donor sets it up in their own bank app.

providers.name: Stripe
providers.tagline: Best engineering platform and by far the cheapest bank transfers, but it cannot do a donor-chosen monthly amount without a workaround.

capabilities.recurringNote: Stripe Payment Links cannot combine a donor-chosen amount with a monthly schedule, so the monthly option is hidden here. See docs/giving-setup.md for the three workarounds.
capabilities.uiNote: Real Stripe Payment Element, rendered in deferred-intent mode from a publishable key alone. It shows the card and US bank account (ACH) tabs exactly as a donor would see them. Validation is Stripe's own; no PaymentIntent is created and nothing is charged.

specs.label: API layer required
specs.value: No for Payment Links; yes to embed checkout on our own page

specs.label: Donor-chosen recurring amount
specs.value: No — needs fixed tiers or a quantity workaround

specs.label: Works on a static site
specs.value: Yes — redirect to a hosted page

caveats: Non-profit processing rates are lower than the list price above, but must be requested once the account is verified.

providers.name: Square
providers.tagline: Lets a donor name their own amount and repeat it monthly with no code — the gap Stripe has. Strongest option if the parish also wants one account for the bookstore and candle desk.

capabilities.uiNote: Square's Web Payments SDK is wired up but stays dormant until `square.applicationId` and `square.locationId` are filled in below. Those are per-account values from the Square Developer Console. Never commit a Square access token.

square.note: From the Square Developer Console. The application ID and location ID are public client-side values; the ACCESS TOKEN is a secret and must never be placed in this repository. Set `environment` to "production" when going live.

specs.label: Recurring donations
specs.value: Yes — donation links take a one-time or recurring frequency

specs.label: Works on a static site
specs.value: Yes — redirect to a hosted page

caveats: The $5,000 cap could block a large building gift. Those would need an invoice instead.
Square's non-profit rate appears to apply to Invoices rather than to all online donations. Confirm before switching.
Best fit if the parish ever wants one system covering the bookstore, candle desk, and online giving.

providers.name: PayPal
providers.tagline: Matches Square on donor-chosen recurring gifts, but keeps the donor on our page instead of redirecting them. Cheapest rail of the three card options on large gifts, once the parish is a confirmed charity.

capabilities.uiNote: PayPal's Donate SDK renders a real button from a hosted button ID, which is a public value rather than a secret. The donation itself happens in a PayPal popup, so no card details and no server are ever involved. It stays a placeholder until `paypal.hostedButtonId` is set, so nobody reviewing this preview can send real money to somebody else's account.

paypal.note: Create the button at paypal.com/donate/buttons and copy its hosted_button_id (business accounts) or use `business` with the account email (personal accounts). Both are public values that appear in the page source by design, so neither is a secret. Enable the recurring option while creating the button: it cannot be turned on from here. Set environment to `sandbox` to test against sandbox.paypal.com.

specs.label: Bank transfer fee
specs.value: Same rate — a bank-funded PayPal gift costs the parish no extra

specs.label: ACH / bank debit
specs.value: Through the donor's PayPal balance or linked bank

specs.label: API layer required
specs.value: No — and unlike Square, without redirecting the donor

specs.label: Recurring donations
specs.value: Yes, monthly, chosen by the donor in the popup

specs.label: Donor-chosen recurring amount
specs.value: Yes — the gap Stripe cannot close

specs.label: Donor self-service
specs.value: Donors cancel or change a recurring gift in their own PayPal account

specs.label: Works on a static site
specs.value: Yes — a popup that keeps the donor on our page

caveats: The 1.99% rate needs PayPal confirmed charity status (PPCC), applied for at paypal.com/charities with proof of registration. Until it is granted the rate is 2.89% + $0.49, which is worse than Stripe.
Recurring has to be switched on when the button is created on PayPal's site. It is not a parameter the SDK can pass, so changing it later means making a new button.

The $0.49 fixed fee is larger than Stripe's or Square's $0.30, so PayPal only wins on larger gifts: it beats Square above about $21, but does not beat Stripe's non-profit rate until about $90. Below that Stripe is cheaper.
Donors without a PayPal account can still pay by card in the popup, but the extra step costs some completion rate compared with a card field sitting on the page.
A donor-chosen amount is entered inside PayPal's popup rather than in the form above, so the amount and fund chosen on this page are passed as a starting point rather than enforced.

providers.name: Zelle
providers.tagline: Genuinely free, which is real money on large gifts — but there is no payment link, so the most a website can do is publish a tag and a QR code to scan.

capabilities.recurringNote: A Zelle standing order is created by the donor in their own banking app. The parish cannot set one up, change it, or cancel it.
capabilities.uiNote: Zelle has no embeddable UI of any kind. The best we can do is show the exact details to copy into a banking app.

specs.label: API layer required
specs.value: None possible — there is no Zelle API for taking payments

specs.label: Recurring donations
specs.value: Only if the donor schedules it in their own bank app

specs.label: Donor-chosen recurring amount
specs.value: Yes, but the parish cannot set it up or change it

specs.label: Automatic receipts
specs.value: None — the treasurer issues them manually

specs.label: Per-transaction cap
specs.value: Set by the donor's bank, often $1,000–$3,500 a day

specs.label: Works on a static site
specs.value: No form to embed; we publish a tag, an address, and a QR code

caveats: There is no Zelle payment link. Nothing on the page can be a clickable “pay now” button, because Zelle has no hosted checkout to link to.

Zelle does support QR codes, but the code must be generated by the parish bank app — it encodes a Zelle directory token and cannot be built from an email address. Export it and set `zelle.qr` to publish it.

A Zelle tag is a business handle (e.g. StElizabethOrthodox) that is friendlier and less error-prone than publishing an email address. It requires a business or non-profit account at a participating bank.
The standalone Zelle app shut down on 1 April 2025, so every donor journey now runs through their own bank's app.
A $5,000 building donation costs about $145 in card fees and nothing by Zelle, so it is worth publishing alongside a card option rather than instead of one.
Not all banks offer Zelle on business or non-profit accounts. Confirm with the parish bank first.
No donor data comes through, so gift-aid style records and year-end statements are entirely manual.
